correlates.name: Pregnancy
correlates.pathophysiology: The gravid uterus compresses the diaphragm from below, reducing both FRC and TLC.

correlates.name: Obesity (and abdominal loading generally)
correlates.pathophysiology: Mass load of adipose tissue surrounding the ribcage and abdomen, plus elevated intra-abdominal pressure transmitted to the chest.

correlates.name: COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease)
correlates.presentation: easily fatigued, frequent respiratory infections, use of accessory muscles to breathe, orthopnea, thin appearance, wheezing, pursed-lip breathing, chronic cough, barrel-shaped chest (classic), dyspnea, prolonged expiratory time, digital clubbing.
correlates.treatment: bronchodilator (albuterol) with repeat spirometry to demonstrate reversible airway obstruction.

correlates.name: Restrictive Lung Disease (pulmonary fibrosis, pneumonia, pulmonary edema)
correlates.presentation: FVC decreased more than FEV1, so FEV1/FVC is preserved or elevated (the lecturer's example, 2.8 ÷ 3.1 ≈ 90%); FRC and RV both decreased.
correlates.pathophysiology: reduced lung compliance increases stiffness and limits expansion; the same elastic recoil that resists filling also drives rapid emptying.

formulas.name: Total Lung Capacity
formulas.meaning: Anchor everything to functional residual capacity, the level the trace returns to after every normal breath — add inspiratory capacity to reach TLC, subtract expiratory reserve volume and only residual volume is left

formulas.name: Functional Residual Capacity
formulas.meaning: The relaxed volume of the lung at the end of a quiet breath, where inward elastic recoil exactly balances outward chest wall recoil
formulas.normalValue: About 2,200 mL; it falls when supine, in obesity, in ascites and in pregnancy, and rises in obstructive disease

formulas.name: FEV1/FVC Ratio
formulas.meaning: The single number that separates obstruction from restriction — obstruction drops it because FEV1 falls far more than FVC, while restriction preserves or raises it because stiff lungs empty fast
formulas.normalValue: About 80% (70% on the guideline cut-off), falling with age; roughly 42% in COPD and 90% in fibrosis

formulas.name: Why Spirometry Cannot Measure RV
formulas.equation: Spirometry measures only voluntarily moved air
formulas.meaning: Residual volume cannot be blown out, so it is unmeasurable by spirometry — and therefore so are the two capacities that contain it, FRC and TLC
formulas.normalValue: RV or FRC must first come from plethysmography, nitrogen washout or helium dilution

formulas.name: Helium Dilution
formulas.equation: C1 x V1 = C2 x (V1 + V2)
formulas.meaning: Helium is not absorbed across the alveolar membrane, so the dilution of a known starting concentration reports the unknown lung volume it mixed into
formulas.normalValue: A worked example gives FRC 3,050 mL and RV 1,850 mL

formulas.name: Dead Space
formulas.equation: Physiologic dead space = anatomic + alveolar dead space
formulas.meaning: Ventilation without perfusion — the anatomic portion is the conducting airways from nose to terminal bronchioles, and the alveolar portion is alveoli that are ventilated but not perfused
formulas.normalValue: Anatomic dead space about 150 mL; it increases with age

formulas.name: Bohr-Enghoff Equation
formulas.meaning: Estimates the dead space fraction from the difference between alveolar and mixed expired CO2, with arterial PaCO2 substituted for alveolar PACO2 in practice
formulas.normalValue: Fowler's nitrogen method gives the anatomic value directly, about 150 mL of a 500 mL tidal volume

formulas.name: Obstructive vs Restrictive PFT Pattern
formulas.equation: Obstructive: FEV1 down hard, ratio down, RV and FRC up. Restrictive: FVC down hard, ratio normal or up, RV and FRC down
formulas.meaning: Obstruction is a problem of getting air out, so volume accumulates; restriction is a problem of getting air in, so every volume falls together
formulas.normalValue: Volumes and capacities run 20-25% lower in women
